record.paper_title: Open problems in the theory of completely positive and copositive matrices
record.original_question: Which algorithms can compute a minimal completely positive factorization of a completely positive matrix A, meaning a factorization A = B B^T with B entrywise nonnegative and with the number of columns of B equal to cpr(A), beyond the few special cases for which such algorithms are already known?

evidence.quote: But only very few algorithms to compute a minimal cp-factorizations were developed so far.

artifact.self_contained_problem: A symmetric matrix $A \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times n}$ is called completely positive if there exists an entrywise nonnegative matrix $B \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times k}$ (for some $k \ge 1$) such that $A = BB^T$. The cp-rank of $A$, denoted $\operatorname{cpr}(A)$, is the smallest such $k$. A factorization $A = BB^T$ with $B \ge 0$ (entrywise) and $B \in \mathbb{R}^{n\times \operatorname{cpr}(A)}$ is called a minimal cp-factorization of $A$.\n\nProblem: Develop algorithms that, given as input a completely positive matrix $A$, compute a minimal cp-factorization $A = BB^T$ (i.e., produce an entrywise nonnegative $B$ whose number of columns equals $\operatorname{cpr}(A)$). The goal is to provide such algorithms beyond the few special cases (such as matrices of small cp-rank, e.g. cp-rank at most 3, or matrices with special combinatorial/structural properties) for which exact procedures are already known. In particular, design a general-purpose, provably correct procedure that determines $\operatorname{cpr}(A)$ and outputs a minimizing nonnegative factor $B$.
artifact.status_search_result: Computing a minimal cp-factorization in general remains an active research problem. Exact finite algorithms are known only in special cases (e.g., Dickinson–Dür's procedure and the algorithm for cp-rank 3 matrices by Brandts/Křížek). More recent works (Groetzner–Dür 2018, Boţ–Nguyen 2021, Riemannian smoothing methods 2022) propose numerical heuristics based on alternating/projected gradient methods, but these do not guarantee minimality of the number of columns in general. No general algorithm with guaranteed minimality is established in the literature.

status_evidence.title: Building a completely positive factorization
status_evidence.snippet: Method based on alternating projections to produce cp-factorizations, without guaranteed minimality in general.
status_evidence.claim: General cp-factorization methods exist but are heuristic, not guaranteed to yield minimal cp-rank factorizations.

status_evidence.title: On the cp-Rank and Minimal cp Factorizations of a Completely Positive Matrix
status_evidence.snippet: Algorithmic procedure for minimal cp factorization (Dickinson and Dür, 2012) handling specific cases.
status_evidence.claim: Known minimal-cp-factorization algorithms are restricted to special cases.

status_evidence.title: Factorization of cp-rank-3 completely positive matrices
status_evidence.snippet: A finite exact algorithm to factorize any matrix of cp-rank 3.
status_evidence.claim: Exact minimal cp-factorization is known for cp-rank ≤ 3.

status_evidence.title: Completely positive factorization by a Riemannian smoothing method
status_evidence.snippet: Riemannian smoothing method for cp-factorization; numerical, no minimality guarantee.
status_evidence.claim: Recent approaches remain numerical heuristics rather than provably minimal algorithms.
